Sports.title: Root won't 'rip up' Bazball blueprint as Babar is ruled out for Pakistan
Sports.content:
Returning England Test skipper Joe Root says he feels "as ready as any other England captain", adding he has no plans on "ripping up" the Bazball blueprint that preceded his second stint in charge.

Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, his first permanent spell from 2017 to 2022 ending with a run of just one win in 17 Tests before Ben Stokes took over in step with head coach Brendon McCullum.

But, after an impressive first couple of years to the Bazball era, the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer saw Stokes retire from international cricket during the final Test and subsequently prompted McCullum's removal as red-ball head coach.

"I don't think there's a huge amount we need to change. It's small things that will make a big difference," Root said ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan, which starts on Wednesday at Headingley - live on Sky Sports Cricket, from 10am (first ball 11am).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"It's not about ripping it up, I think it's about keeping a lot of the good stuff we've been doing for a period of time, stuff that Ben and Baz built for a long while.

"I don't believe there is one way of playing Test cricket. You've got to be adaptable and play the situation. It's never the same throughout five days, there's different challenges and you've got to adjust to the ebbs and flows throughout."

As for his own readiness to return to the captaincy, the 35-year-old made it clear he was fully prepared to embrace the challenge one more time.

"The landscape is different," he said. "I'm a different player and person than I was when I [first] took over as captain.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Cricket podcast, Nasser Hussain fears Joe Root sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes

"I'm in a very fortunate, unique position where I've got 60-odd games of experience to look back on. There are things I might want to change and do slightly differently.

"I had time to step away, play in a different environment, under a different coach, different captain, and see the game from a different lens.

"In many ways I feel as ready as any other England captain that's been before; to have that amount of experience is invaluable."

He added: "I'm really excited. And to get the chance to start at Headingley as well is always nice, my home ground.

"It's a very talented group of players that are very capable of special things. I'm really excited about where we can take this team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew previously imposed on his team

'Hugely supportive' Brook to remain vice-captain

White-ball skipper Harry Brook, despite serving as Test vice-captain, was overlooked in favour of Root to lead England in Stokes' absence for the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval, as well as for the permanent job upon his international retirement.

Root confirmed Brook will continue in the role as No 2 in the Test team and insisted the pair's bond remains strong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Nasser Hussain, believes Harry Brook is a 'very good captain' but needs the 'mature Harry to come out' after his England Test captaincy snub

"Our relationship is exactly as it has been for a long time," he said. "Me and Harry are very good friends and get along well away from cricket, and clearly get the best out of each other when playing together.

"He's been hugely supportive. I fully feel like he's got my back, as the rest of the guys do. He's going to be invaluable.

"He's done some brilliant things already within the white-ball space. He's a brilliant leader within the group and the fact he's not captain, that shouldn't be taken away from him."

As for life without Stokes, Root added: "It's a big void to fill. He's someone who has been ever present for the best part of 15 years.

"It's been different, but we've only been together as a full team for a day and a half."

And quizzed on whether he could yet return to the side, with a home Ashes series on the horizon in 2027, Root said: "Who knows? That's a question for Ben.

"We need to look after the here and now, and that's this series."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key does not rule out a return to Test cricket for Ben Stokes and why they chose to appoint Joe Root as captain and not Harry Brook

Pakistan captain Babar injured for Headingley

Pakistan captain Babar Azam has been ruled out of the series opener against England due to a finger injury, with Salman Ali Agha taking temporary charge at Headingley.

Image: Pakistan captain Babar Azam will miss the first Test at Headingley due to an injured finger

Babar was initially struck on the right hand when facing the West Indies earlier this month, before he then received another blow from England Under-19 seamer Manny Lumsden in a tour match at Beckenham last week. He retired hurt in what was described at the time as a "precautionary measure".

The tourists were keen to give him time to recover but, while he has been cleared of a broken middle finger, he has not been cleared to lead his side at Headingley despite working through a brief net session.

"Babar Azam is not available, Salman will be captain," head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said on Tuesday.

"It's not broken, there is a little bit of swelling on the finger. Hopefully he will be available for the second Test match."

Babar's absence robs Pakistan not only of their leader but one of their most talented batters, with nine Test hundreds to his name and a Test average of 43.68. Saud Shakeel is expected to be drafted into the XI after sitting out the West Indies series.

'Relaxed Root looks up for the challenge'

Sky Sports News reporter James Cole:

"It's old shoes for Joe Root; he's got all the experience behind him and he seemed relaxed.

"He is, it's fair to say, inheriting a big rebuilding job. England have lost seven of their last 10 Tests, they've lost their head coach Brendon McCullum and their captain Ben Stokes, who had been such a mainstay of the Test team for so long and led such a unique, attacking brand of cricket called Bazball.

Image: Jordan Cox comes into England's side for just his second Test

"As well as losing Stokes from the middle order, who was the glue and provided balance between the batting and bowling, they've got an opener Emilio Gay who has played just three Test and who is out of nick at the moment, and a rookie at number three in Jordan Cox, who has only batted there once before.

"In place of the talismanic Stokes, Dan Lawrence comes back in and offers a spinning all-rounder option, but he hasn't played a Test in two years.

"It's fair to say Root has got a lot on his hands, but he's up for the challenge."

Sports.title: Rodri completes Barcelona move as Man City pursue replacement
Sports.content:
Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m.

The Spain World Cup winner and former Ballon d'Or winner, who helped City win four Premier League titles and a Champions League crown, has signed a four-year contract with the LaLiga club.

Rodri, 30, had one year left on his City contract and, while they wanted him to stay and sign an extension, Barcelona's third offer proved to be too good to turn down.

Barcelona had bids of £40m and £55m rejected by City before the deal was eventually agreed.

Enzo Maresca's side are pursuing replacements for both Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders, who is set to join Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for around £51m.

IN FULL: Rodri pens City farewell to fans

"Dear City fans, I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try," it said, on the club's official website.

"It's hard to find the words to express how much gratitude, love and support me and my family have experienced all these years.

"And then Pep, waiting to teach me everything from day one. Pep I can tell you now, I couldn't handle all those tactics in my head.

"But a question came to me, 'could we handle all these expectations for the next years.' I think that time answered the question.

"I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect. We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it. And the fans were with us every step of the way.

"Many incredible moments come to my mind.

"My first trophy at City, in my first game.

"The last minute winners, like Arsenal away.

"Scoring in the Villa game to reach the Premier League, when it looked so tough.

"Scoring the goal to win the Champions League that we all wanted so much.

"The incredible reception you gave me after the Balon d'Or. You cannot imagine how proud I am to be the first player to win this award in a sky blue shirt.

"Making history, with the Treble, with Four in a Row. We saw things they'll never see.

"And in the bad moments, also, you never let me down. My first day back on the pitch I realised how much you love me and I understood how special these fans were.

"City didn't just make me a grow as a player. They made me grow as a human.

"I saw my brother graduating from Manchester Metropolitan University.

"I could see my girlfriend working for the NHS.

"Manchester shaped my whole life.

"I will never forget stepping onto the pitch, seeing a sea of blue sing 'nah, nah, nah, nah…CITY', taking my scooter into town for a coffee, walking through the parks listening to Oasis and always loving Manchester's great rain.

"So City fans, it's time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my teammates. This journey couldn't be the same without you, my heart will always be Blue."

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 15: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 2nd (NB: this is not necessarily Jamie Jackson’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 2nd

Prospects

Enzo Maresca was already in herculean task mode by signing on as the man charged with continuing the dynasty built by Pep Guardiola at Manchester City before Rodri decided to leave the club and join Barcelona. The 30-year-old may be headed for a second Ballon d’Or after his displays in Spain’s triumphant World Cup campaign, so the loss of a midfielder capable of moulding games domestically and in the Champions League represents a sizeable blow for Maresca.

There are further negatives too, with John Stones, Nathan Aké and Bernardo Silva also no longer at City. On the positive side, Elliot Anderson has joined for £116m from Nottingham Forest having impressed for England at the World Cup. City’s new manager also has Erling Haaland, who will be favourite to claim a fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons. Less certain is how Phil Foden will perform despite being boosted by a bumper new contract. Can the boy from Stockport dovetail with Rayan Cherki and once more pull the strings for his boyhood side?

Off-field picture

City are a best-in-class organisation, who can be used as an exemplar of how to pursue excellence on and off the field. This, of course, would change were they found guilty over the 130 charges brought against them for alleged breaches of Premier League rules. It has been more than three years since the charges were announced, with City continuing to deny any wrongdoing. The new Pep Guardiola Stand, opened for the great man’s final home game last season, means 61,000 fans can now witness Haaland and co go to work, the Etihad Stadium’s capacity having previously stood at 53,400.

Owner-fan relationship

Sheikh Mansour is a hero to the City faithful for a glittering period of ownership that has elevated their team to a domestic and continental superpower. Listening to fans, the club have also frozen ticket prices for a third consecutive season. Meanwhile in the Pep Guardiola Stand, 4,000 new flexi season tickets – a pay-as-you-go scheme – have sold out, half of which are for junior fans, with City introducing £10 seats for those who live in the five wards around the ground.

The manager

Is Maresca courageous for following The Man or naive for believing he can? Over to the 46-year-old, who has zero doubt the City job is no chalice laced with poison. “It’s fantastic, nice and exciting, and for me, a privilege,” he said. “First of all, the most important thing has been that Khaldoon [al-Mubarak, the chair], Hugo [Viana, the director of football] and Ferran [Soriano, the chief executive] all speak the same language in terms of this is a club that has to win games, titles and has to compete, but we also talk about how we can continue to make this club better, season after season.” Maresca’s CV shows the Championship crown with Leicester, and the Conference League and Club World Cup glory with Chelsea. How he would love to add the Premier League title to that roll of honour at the first time of asking.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson of Manchester City holds off Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly of Arsenal during the 2026 FA Community Shield. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

Rodri’s departure offers Anderson an opportunity to run City’s midfield. Can he do so? Maresca and Viana obviously believe this or £116m would not have been splurged on the lad from Whitley Bay who could not nail down a starting berth for Newcastle in five years as a senior professional there. At the World Cup there were flashes of a schemer who can spray passes long range – Rodri-style – as well as the shorter, metronomic stuff. What’s for sure is that Anderson has a career-defining opportunity in front of him.

Stat attack

Manchester City conceded more league goals from set pieces last season than they had in the previous two campaigns combined. They were costly at times too: the winning goals in their losses at Aston Villa and Newcastle both came from corners, for instance. Maresca’s Chelsea conceded from a set play every three league games so his record there was a shade worse than City’s in 2025-26. He has work to do.

Set for a breakthrough

Vitor Reis was signed in January 2025 and made four appearances that season. The defender’s debut was also forgettable as, then 19, he was hooked at half-time with City trailing 1-0 at Leyton Orient in the FA Cup fourth round. The Brazilian played all of the 3-1 victory in the following round, and was fielded in the 89th-minute of the 2-0 league victory at Leicester in April before his sole other City appearance: a full outing in the 2-0 Club World Cup win over Wydad Casablanca that June. Last season’s loan at City’s sister club Girona ended in relegation, but Reis is said to have impressed.

World Cup impact

The departed Rodri made real the ultimate fantasy of all players by captaining his country to the World Cup and being so vital to that glory that he was named player of the tournament. Cherki fared less well, making six substitute appearances and one start for a France side that fell, to Spain, in the semi-finals. France’s attacking ranks may overflow with quality, but for a player with magic in both boots, that seemed odd.

Sports.title: Israel withdraws support for embattled Fifa president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s decision to sack his chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after the Frenchman’s criticism of the World Cup sell-off plan has hardened some opposition to the Fifa president, with the efforts to force him out expected to intensify over the next few days.

On Tuesday Israel became the latest Fifa member to officially withdraw their support for Infantino’s re-election in a letter sent by the head of the Israel Football Association (IFA), Moshe Zuares.

The move is not a surprise as the IFA has been a member of Uefa since 1994 and Zuares sits on the European governing body’s executive committee, but it remains another blow to Infantino, who has invested significant political capital in attempting to improve sporting relations with Palestine.

At Fifa’s congress in April Infantino tried to stage a photo involving the two delegations in Vancouver, but the Palestinian Football Federation president, Jibril Rajoub, refused to stand alongside IFA ⁠vice-president, Basim Sheikh ⁠Suliman. Undeterred by this setback, Infantino wants Israel and Palestine to compete in the first match of a new under-15 tournament in the United States next month, as reported by the Guardian in June.

In his letter, which has been seen by the Guardian, Zuares says recent events have triggered an “unprecedented crisis of confidence” between the visions of Uefa and Fifa when it comes to global governance, adding that the rift is “profound, substantive, and principled, and compelling all stakeholders to reconsider the path forward”.

In a decision he described as being taken unanimously after a meeting of the IFA’s board, Zuares confirmed: “We have no choice but to retract our previous letter of support, in the sincere hope that fruitful dialogue among all parties will eventually restore a shared, proper vision and direction for world football.”

Israeli’s intervention echoes the withdrawal of support from other Uefa members including England, Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland, and followed confirmation on Monday night that Lamour had left Fifa, having been deeply critical of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

“If that means I lose my job, then so be it,” he said prophetically in a statement on 31 July. “I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

Another Uefa executive committee member, the former Wales Women international Laura McAllister, said the decision to sack Lamour “sends a deeply troubling message” and casts serious doubt over any efforts by the global governing body to recalibrate after the FFE scandal.

McAllister, who is one of five Uefa vice-presidents and worked there with Lamour before his move to Fifa in 2024, praised her former colleague for standing up to Infantino’s doomed scheme. “During the shabby events of the past weeks, he showed himself to be a courageous advocate for the most important stakeholders in football,” she said in a statement. “Kevin’s sacking seriously weakens Fifa’s administration, while undermining this unique opportunity to shift the culture at Fifa and to reset the organisation on sporting values, not simply commercial and financial ones.

“Fifa is not the president, it is the whole football family. As I have said repeatedly, world football needs strong, principled, independent leaders who are prepared to speak up, challenge when necessary, and stand firmly by their values and those of the global game. Instead, the loss of a leader of Kevin’s calibre sends a deeply troubling message to all of us seeking change.”

View image in fullscreen Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, said: ‘I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup.’ Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Meanwhile, Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, told the BBC that Infantino pressed the “self-destruct button” over his botched plan to bring private investment into the World Cup.

“This is a problem of Fifa’s making,” Masters said. “This is a self-inflicted wound. The organisation has pressed the self-destruct button, and the consequences of that flow now into the solutions that need to be found.

“I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup. They’re a not-for-profit organisation. They should really be holding that competition in trust for the future of football.”

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos consortium could be majority Liverpool shareholder within a year
Sports.content:
1892 Holdings, the new investor in Liverpool, has first refusal to become the majority shareholder in the next 12 months should Fenway Sports Group decide to sell.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia and including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was believed to have bought 30% to one-third of Liverpool when the deal was announced on Friday. However, the agreement is for 38% of the Anfield club, meaning 1892 has paid FSG just over £2bn to become a minority shareholder. The increased stake, first reported by the Athletic, still values Liverpool at about £5.5bn.

FSG also insisted on Friday the deal with 1892 was not part of an exit strategy from a club it bought for £300m in 2010 and it was not compelled to sell more of Liverpool to the consortium at a future date. That remains the case but should FSG decide to sell or reduce its shareholding in the next 12 months, then 1892 has an agreement in place that gives it the option to buy a controlling stake.

Liverpool’s majority owner has stressed it is an option for 1892 over the next 12 months, one that could lead to further investment, and is not a formal commitment on its part. FSG remains in operational control of Liverpool. But it does raise the possibility of Bezos, Bhatia and the Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, another billionaire member of the consortium, replacing FSG as Liverpool’s majority shareholders in the near future.

Bezos, one of the richest men in the world, is deemed a passive investor in Liverpool at this stage, having bought into 1892 through the K5 Sports fund, of which he is the lead investor. Bryan Baum, the co-founder and managing partner of K5 Global, will have a seat on an expanded Liverpool board alongside Bhatia as vice-chair and Elaine Saverin, wife of Eduardo. Bhatia has received financial backing from the Mittal Family Trust to buy into Liverpool. His father-in-law is the Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, another billionaire. The Mittal family are worth around $17bn and Saverin an estimated $33bn.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s boardroom rift: if Boehly goes who will Clearlake have left to blame? | Sam Cunningham
Sports.content:
Perhaps, in hindsight, it was always going to end this way. As some of the world’s wealthiest investors scrambled to find funds after Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine set a series of dominoes toppling that forced Roman Abramovich to sell Chelsea, it threw together some unexpected allies.

Todd Boehly became the public face of the winning bid, convincing the US sports mogul Mark Walter and the Swiss businessman Hansjörg Wyss to join as 12.8% minority investors. The private equity firm Clearlake Capital put in 61.6%, bringing the owners Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, who made their fortunes investing in tech, into the leadership fold.

But once the adrenaline rush of beating 11 serious rivals in an expedited bid process run by the Raine Group had worn off, that was really when the problems started. Now they actually owned Chelsea, how were they going to run it? What was the strategy? How would they tackle a stadium falling well behind their rivals?

Maybe Abramovich made running Chelsea look easier than it was. The club had not finished outside the top five for six seasons, yet in the four seasons since the takeover, their average league position is eighth – with a high of fourth and a low of 12th. Possibly the conflicting opinions of people who always think they are right, and have the money to prove it, is not the optimal setup.

Before the takeover, an agreement was struck that Boehly, representing Walter and Wyss, would have final signoff on major decisions alongside Eghbali and Feliciano. Over the years, Boehly and Eghbali have been the dominant day-to-day decision-makers at the club, while the others remained largely silent partners, insulated from the fan anger and social media ridicule that inevitably follows any period of struggle.

Some sources maintain that Boehly and Eghbali share a “professional” relationship, but signs of strain had leaked into the public domain long before this week’s revelation that Boehly and Walter were open to selling their stakes to Clearlake in a deal that would value the club at about £5bn.

In May 2024 Boehly told the Qatar Economic Forum that “patience” with the project was essential. Mauricio Pochettino had just led Chelsea to the EFL Cup final, the FA Cup semi-final and they had recovered from a poor start to finish sixth. Cole Palmer was a breakout star; Reece James was made captain. They won their last five games of the season.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso is aiming to rediscover the momentum Chelsea had built under Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Paul Dennis/TGS Photo/Shutterstock

Six days later, Pochettino was gone – dismissed after the co-sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart compiled an 18-page review of the season.

Another glimpse of the pervading tension – and possibly a hint at what was to come – emerged in March last year in Boehly’s Bloomberg interview discussing the slow-moving stadium development plans, four years after they were announced.

“We have to think long term about what we’re trying to accomplish,” Boehly said. “We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out. That’s going to be where we’re either aligned or we ultimately decide to go different ways.”

Publicly, Boehly insisted the ownership was aligned. Yet that is also at odds with how it began: the American installing himself as sporting director and driving a £250m spending spree targeting experienced players such as Raheem Sterling and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Chelsea finished 12th.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Boehly then stepped back, with Eghbali taking a more active role. About 70 interviews took place to build a new football structure, resulting in the appointments of Winstanley and Stewart – later promoted to co-sporting directors – and Joe Shields, now a co-director of recruitment.

They attempted to redefine how a football club is run: buying young, handing out unusually long contracts, in a model that has fascinated and baffled many in football. As an indication of how well that’s gone, in 2024 fans placed stickers around Stamford Bridge mocking up the three owners as clowns, while the Chelsea Supporters’ Trust described their club as “a laughing stock”.

The spending has been unprecedented – the pre-tax loss of £262.4m in the year ending June 2025 was a Premier League record supporters had probably not envisaged after Boehly declared the owners’ vision was “to make the fans proud” after the takeover. They have complied with Premier League spending restrictions only by effectively selling the women’s side to themselves. But it could not stop a significant fine for breaching Uefa’s financial rules, which did not permit the club to include the sale as income.

But there have been signs that the grand plan(s) will work. Momentum grew under Enzo Maresca Chelsea qualified for the Champions League and lifted the Club World Cup, and there was frustration that last season was derailed by his abrupt departure in January, after which they plummeted from Champions League contenders to 10th.

Now comes another reset under Xabi Alonso and a new strategy tweak towards older, more tried and tested players. But the boardroom drama persists. Both sides have explored buying each other out in recent years, but it appears Boehly’s and Walter’s hands have been forced. Walter, a long-term friend and business partner of Boehly, is under investigation by the US Department of Justice for alleged tax fraud and is believed to be selling assets to pay loans facing federal attention. He unexpectedly sold the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5bn (£9.2bn) last week and his Chelsea stake could be next.

An exit would coincide neatly with Boehly’s five-year tenure as Chelsea chair coming to an end at the conclusion of this season and a representative from Clearlake ready to fill his place. If a sale is agreed, Eghbali and Feliciano will have full control – and no one else to blame if things don’t improve.

Sports.title: Barcelona steal Rodri away from Real Madrid and plan to make him new Busquets
Sports.content:
By the time Flight PTN27B started its descent into El Prat a bit before 8pm on Monday evening, a small crowd had gathered by the terminal doors, waiting for it to land. A few people stood and watched the sky, cameras out to capture its arrival. A lot more watched on their phones. In the two hours it had taken to get there from Manchester, taking off at 5.11pm, 101 minutes behind schedule, the Pilatus PC-24 had become the most tracked plane on the planet. Everyone knew that Rodrigo Hernández was on board. Unless, of course, he had been sneaked away in a catering cart.

Five days earlier, Rodri had been seen, and recorded, at Barajas airport waiting to get on a flight back to Manchester from Madrid. He wheeled a small RFEF (Spanish football federation) case with his name on, stood alone in the queue, the World Cup-winning captain just a bloke in shorts and T-shirt, and his stay in the UK was supposed to be brief, just long enough to say goodbye. The plane he was boarding was a Ryanair one: that was the detail everyone homed in on, something extraordinary in the ordinariness. This time, though, he came on a private jet, one way. His family travelled with him. He came to sign for FC Barcelona.

Rodri was late: an agreement between Manchester City and Barcelona had taken a little longer than expected, long enough for concern to creep in, and his flight landed 70 minutes behind schedule. Maybe he is late-late, too: at 30, and three years after the departure of Sergio Busquets – the man to whom he had always been likened and whose natural successor he has always been … this transfer could perhaps have come sooner. Yet it was rarely even contemplated, virtually up until the moment it happened. In that sense, it had actually been quick. A fortnight ago, few thought of this.

Now here he was, heading out in jeans and a white T-shirt. There was expectation, a hint still of disbelief that they had got him. A touch of relief, too, after the delay. They had been “intense days”, Rodri said, but now it was done. Barcelona’s third bid had been accepted: €60m plus a further €15m in add-ons, €11m of which are virtually guaranteed. He will earn around €15m a year, an increase on his salary at City, and has signed a four-year deal.

Quick Guide Rodri seals Barcelona transfer Show The Spain midfielder Rodri has completed his €60m move from Manchester City to Barcelona, signing a four-year contract after undergoing a medical on Tuesday. "Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement for Rodri, who is committing to the Catalan club until 30 June 2030," read a club statement. Barça added that the 30-year-old is "considered one of the best players in the world in his position", and "stands out for his tactical intelligence, composure on the ball, ability to regain possession and precision in his passing". Rodri (pictured) was named the best player of the World Cup after Spain’s triumph this summer. He spent seven seasons at the Etihad Stadium, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the winner in the 2023 Champions League final against Inter. The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner joined from Atlético Madrid in July 2019, and was in the final year of his contract. In a message to City fans on the club’s website, Rodri wrote: "I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try. I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made – winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect. "We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it," he added. "And the fans were with us every step of the way. City didn’t just make me grow as a player. They made me grow as a human ... Manchester shaped my whole life. It’s time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my teammates. This journey couldn’t be the same without you, my heart will always be blue." Barcelona saw an initial £40m offer and an increased bid turned down before an agreement was struck on Sunday. Rodri flew to Barcelona’s El Prat airport on Monday and told reporters: "Playing for Barcelona is a dream come true for me." The new City manager, Enzo Maresca, faces a race to rebuild his midfield, with Rodri joining Bernardo Silva in departing the club, Tijjani Reijnders poised to join Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah, and Newcastle reportedly interested in Nico González. Elliot Anderson has joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m and City have been linked with Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández. Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I’m happy to be here,” Rodri said, and they were happy to have him. The following morning he arrived at the club’s Joan Despí training ground to complete his medical, everything signed off. As he left the terminal building, Rodri had been asked if this was a dream come true. He of course said yes it was, which he had to say. The question had been direct, leading. It had been loaded too.

A Ballon d’Or winner and the embodiment of a style, an identity, that is theirs too, Rodri is the perfect fit. The time was right for him too. Voted the best player at the World Cup, the culmination of his recovery from injury, there was just one year left on his contract at City. He had won it all in England and Pep Guardiola had gone. After seven years away, home called. But home didn’t mean Barcelona; in fact, it had seemed more likely to mean Real Madrid.

View image in fullscreen Rodri lifts the World Cup after Spain’s victory over Argentina. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Rodri grew up to the north-west of the capital and even Real’s refusal to turn up the night he won the Ballon d’Or, an act of grubbiness and disrespect, didn’t mean closing the door. Instead, he was increasingly open about his willingness – his apparent desire – to go. “Obviously, when the best club in history, the most successful with everything that brings, call you it is an honour and you always have to pay attention,” he said not long after the ceremony. In the spring, Rodri admitted he would like to return to Spain and that he would not rule out going to Real, even if he had been in the academy at Atlético. When Real held presidential elections in May, the pretender, Enrique Riquelme, announced that his signing would be Rodri. For his part, Rodri kept his counsel and come the end of the World Cup he had three offers: Paris Saint-Germain, who he ruled out because he wanted a return to Spain, Barcelona and Real.

Real, ambivalent before, appeared convinced by his status as the World Cup’s best player, president Florentino Pérez’s reticence seemingly overcome. He was exactly the footballer they needed, someone to get them to actually play, and Real were confident that he would come, that theirs was the only real offer. One headline summed it up: “Rodri is next”. This was done, which is when things tend to get undone. Rodri had an offer that was impossible to turn down. Only the terms of the negotiation shifted, doubts growing about Real’s commitment, frustration growing.

Barcelona, seeing an opportunity, pushed at an unexpectedly opening door. Rodri might not have been the player they needed most – a forward was their priority – but, well, he’s Rodri. This was undeniably a step up in quality, even for a midfield like theirs. Meanwhile, doubts over Frenkie de Jong’s fitness brought a reframing: maybe he was more necessary than they had believed. Likewise, that slight nagging doubt about his fit with Pedri in the selección feels like a small one, easily overcome, certainly no obstacle to bringing together arguably the best two midfielders in the world. Good luck getting the ball off them.

On the day that Real announced Vinícius Júnior had renewed his contract at the club and that they had made Yan Diomande the most expensive signing in their history, they also briefed that Rodri wasn’t coming after all. The excitement among fans at the Santiago Bernabéu turned to disappointment, a kind of lingering doom. That huge hole in the middle of Madrid’s midfield was still not plugged, their issues still not addressed.

View image in fullscreen Rodri enjoyed seven successful seasons at Manchester City. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

For Barcelona this was the signing of the summer. The World Cup winning-captain, perhaps the best player on the planet, was coming to Catalonia. There was a kind of gleeful disbelief, the expectation huge. Rodri thanked Madrid, but he had made his decision. As usual, Jorge Valdano put it best when the €75m deal had been done. “Rodri’s deal is worth €35m for what it gives Barcelona and €40m for what it takes away from Madrid,” he said. “At Real Madrid he would have revolutionised their play and improved everything.”

Valdano added he will not have the impact on Barcelona’s style that he would have had on Real’s, but that was because it is already his. “I always try to learn from Busquets,” said Rodri. “I watched him especially closely: he, and others, laid down a model of playing I knew I had to follow.” When Rodri joined City, Guardiola had found his other Busquets, or so it goes. Waiting patiently for his moment, when Busquets finally left the national team, it was always going to be Rodri who stepped in. A “perfect computer”, Luis de la Fuente called him. Doing so with Barcelona would seem natural, maybe even overdue, his signing a no-brainer.

Rodri’s World Cup overcame any doubts that it was too late, that his time had gone, and brought an extra dimension too, a shift in his role which he didn’t just embrace but consciously sought. He had the maturity, the leadership, the ascendancy over Spain’s young players – Barcelona’s young players – that they needed. And he needed too: there is something almost paternal about him and they had the youth that he wanted to lead, to guide. And, of course, the talent too. He knows how good it is to play with them: he had done so all summer, winning the ultimate award. And so it was done.

Now all that was needed was for City and Barcelona to reach an agreement. Eventually, they did, so Rodrigo Hernández had another plane to catch.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala says ‘treatable seizures’ are reason for two collapses in four days
Sports.content:
The Bayern Munich winger Jamal Musiala has revealed he is suffering from “treatable absence seizures” after he collapsed on the pitch for the second time in four days.

Musiala fell to the floor eight minutes after coming on as a substitute in Bayern’s friendly with Heidenheim on Tuesday night. The 23-year-old experienced a similar incident during Saturday’s friendly against RB Leipzig, but Musiala has insisted there is no long-term health risk.

“First things first, I am doing well. I am incredibly grateful for your messages and your support!” Musiala posted on Instagram. “I understand that many of you are worried. I would like to put those concerns to rest today and explain the situation.

“I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary – but treatable – absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction. These can lead to the kind of incidents seen recently, such as during the match against Leipzig or the game in Heidenheim.

“I know they might look alarming at first glance, but for me, they are currently part of my everyday life. I am receiving excellent medical care and remain very optimistic. FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this. Importantly, there is no further health risk involved.”

View image in fullscreen Jamal Musiala also had to leave the field during Bayern Munich’s friendly win over RB Leipzig on Saturday. Photograph: Midori Ikenouchi/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

The Germany international added: “In close consultation and regular contact with the experts, it was my personal wish to face this challenge; with the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery most: simply living my life and pursuing my passion for playing football.”

Having come on for Ismael Saibari after 61 minutes against Heidenheim, Musiala was replaced by Cassiano Kiala eight minutes later. He appeared dazed as he received medical treatment and was helped off the pitch, with Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, moving to play down concerns soon after the game.

“Jamal will speak about this in the near future. We knew about it and we are aware of the situation,” Eberl said.

Bayern won the game 4-2, with Felipe Chávez, Arijon Ibrahimovic, Luis Díaz and Nathaniel Brown all on target. Musiala also required medical attention after collapsing in the match against RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Dedic completes £29.5m Newcastle move, Wan-Bissaka loaned to Villa
Sports.content:
The chance to be reunited with Matthias Jaissle convinced Amar Dedic to swap Benfica for Newcastle in a £29.5m transfer. Dedic becomes Newcastle’s sixth signing of a turbulent summer on Tyneside and the 24-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international is likely to start at right‑back at home to Liverpool on Sunday.

“Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me,” said Dedic, who played for Newcastle’s new manager at RB Salzburg. “We know each other well; he knows what I can bring to the pitch and I’m really happy to play for him again. It’s a special feeling and a real honour to join Newcastle.”

With Tino Livramento still recovering from a calf injury, Newcastle’s lack of senior right-backs has been highlighted in pre-season and, soon after replacing Eddie Howe this month, Jaissle advised club executives that Dedic could fill the void. It helps that a defender also comfortable at left-back understands the German’s playing philosophy.

Newcastle are also talking to Manchester City about the possibility of signing the midfielder Nico González, having lost Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães.

Aston Villa have agreed a deal with West Ham to sign Aaron Wan-Bissaka on loan with an option to make his move permanent at the end of the season. Villa had an initial offer to take Wan-Bissaka on a straight loan rejected by West Ham. The Democratic Republic of the Congo defender will provide Unai Emery with cover for Matty Cash. Villa are also hoping to sign João Palhinha and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over the Portugal midfielder.

Brighton have signed the Canada forward Promise David from Union Saint-Gilloise on a season-long loan, with the move becoming permanent if certain conditions are met.

Juventus have signed Guglielmo Vicario from Tottenham on a season-long loan. The deal includes an option for Juve to make the goalkeeper’s move permanent at the end of ​the season, ‌Tottenham said. Vicario, ‌29, joined Spurs from Empoli ‌in 2023 and has made 117 appearances for the north London club. He was part of the side ‌that won the Europa League in 2025, ending the ​club’s 17-year wait for a major trophy, but lost his place to Antonin Kinsky after the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi as manager in March.

Sunderland were set to announce their acquisition of a new left-back after fending off competition from Roma and Newcastle to win the race to sign the Toulouse defender Dayann Methalie for £25.6m, but that transfer was on hold on Tuesday night after it emerged that the 20-year-old had failed part of his medical. Sunderland’s specialists are believed to have detected a potential back problem and the defender has now returned to Toulouse, where an independent French consultant is set to examine him.

A France Under-21s international, Metahlie made 28 Ligue One appearances last season and has been lined up to compete with Reinildo for a place in Régis Le Bris’s starting XI. Methalie, who had been about to sign a five-year contract at the Stadium of Light, is also comfortable operating as a left-sided central defender or wingback.

Harry Kane, meanwhile, has said “now is the time to start talking” about signing a new deal at Bayern Munich. The 33-year-old is entering the last season of his initial four-year deal at the Bundesliga champions.

Sports.title: In Zavier Gozo, Crystal Palace land a US prospect living up to the hype
Sports.content:
For much of the past year, the story of American starlet Zavier Gozo has been one of realizing potential – even in failure. Speaking with the Guardian the day after he and Real Salt Lake teammate Diego Luna learned they wouldn’t be on Mauricio Pochettino’s squad for this summer’s World Cup, the 19-year-old Gozo admitted the rejection made him realize how close he’d gotten to earning a spot.

“I thought I would be less disappointed than I was,” Gozo said in May. “Obviously, it wasn’t like I was supposed to go. I feel like I was disappointed, but I also think it just gave me so much more motivation to be able to make the first team, whenever that is.”

If it works out well, Gozo’s move to Crystal Palace could see that happen sooner than many would have anticipated a year ago. The Premier League club finalized the transfer of Gozo from Real Salt Lake on Tuesday in a five-year deal. The agreement is reportedly worth around $15m (£11m).

The move follows one of the most rapid ascents of any American men’s prospect in recent memory.

Gozo joined the Real Salt Lake academy in 2021 at age 14, debuting with their second team, Real Monarchs, a year later. His MLS debut came in 2023, when he was still just 16. Over time, Gozo emerged as an option at right wing-back offering precocious confidence on the ball, capping his first full season with RSL with four goals and three assists in 1,810 minutes.

This season, Gozo has been given increased license to stay upfield. His technique in close quarters has been especially impressive, with deft touches and passes helping RSL get into dangerous areas. His end product has also been on greater display, with six goals and five assists in 1,417 minutes thus far.

Zavier Gozo Real Salt Lake highlights

His ability to set up his own shot as well as create dangerous looks for his teammates helps him stand out. Gozo has made 67 progressive carries upfield, per Futi, a category led by Lionel Messi, Denis Bouanga, Evander and Anders Dreyer – four members of last year’s MLS Best XI.

The question for any young player of Gozo’s caliber is how best to position themselves for international consideration. On the one hand, he had already established himself as a regular starter in MLS. On the other, strong performances in MLS – as in any league – provide no guarantee of landing on a national team, as Gozo’s teammate Luna learned the hard way by being among Pochettino’s toughest omissions.

As a result, Gozo felt he was nearing the ideal window for making a move across the Atlantic.

“I feel like I’m ready to go,” Gozo added without hesitation. “Whether that happens or not, I don’t know, but I think this is a unique situation I have. I’m blessed to be in a situation where I have such a good club to be at, but I also think, you know … What’s next in my career? I don’t know.”

The son of an American mother and an Ivorian father, Gozo also earned his first US youth international callup in 2022, beginning with the U-15s. He has become a regular with the youth national teams.

With Pochettino opting to stick with the USMNT through the 2030 World Cup, Gozo figures to be in contention with the players who made the squad for this summer’s tournament for a place in the US’s plans over the next four years. Training at Palace every day with US mainstay Chris Richards will surely keep him in Pochettino’s sights, to say nothing of any Premier League minutes he’s able to get under new manager Pierre Sage.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta hints at more Arsenal signings and reveals ‘important’ Pep Guardiola talk ahead Premier League title defence
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola may have left the Premier League but his influence will remain for years to come, according to Mikel Arteta.

The Arsenal boss is ready to launch his side’s title defence but not before a quick pep talk with the former Manchester City manager.



3 Arteta and Guardiola went from colleagues to title rivals Credit: Getty

The Gunners face Coventry in their Premier League opener on Friday evening – live on talkSPORT – hoping to pick up from where they left off last season.

And that was putting Guardiola’s Manchester City side in their place to claim a first title in 22 years.

Arteta’s ex-mentor Guardiola called time on his decade-long tenure at the Etihad Stadium in May and the Arsenal boss admits it was strange not to see his compatriot on the sidelines during last Sunday’s Community Shield between the two clubs.



Not facing Guadiola was a bizarre feeling

"It was different," Arteta told talkSPORT. "Obviously I know Enzo [Maresca] really well but obviously the relationship I built with Pep when we were with each other.

"The amount of headaches and sweats he has provided to me over the last six or seven years to try to catch their level.



"He’s been an absolute inspiration, he's left a mark on this league forever and he made all of us better.

Asked whether he had spoken to Guardiola since his side’s title triumph, Arteta said: “I have and I’m due to have an important one in the next few days and I’m looking forward to it."



Ahead of the new season, Arteta admits he is excited at the prospect of creating further history for the north London club.

The Gunners have never achieved back-to-back Premier League titles – a feat achieved by only Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho and Guardiola.

But Arteta has shrugged off the notion of achieving personal accolades and claims that any targets for the season will be collective ones.

3 Arteta is aiming for a repeat of last season's title success Credit: Getty



“I’m very excited. We already have some dreams about the competition again with the Community Shield. It’s a new season, new expectations,” he added.

“We have the opportunity to do something we haven't done before at this football club, to win it back to back and that is the ambition.

“It’s not personal, it’s the collective ambition that we have and the ambition of the club.

“It's a beautiful challenge. When you know how to do it and to replicate it, the challenge will be different. The things we will face along the journey will be different.



“I feel very confident we are going to give ourselves a big chance to be there again.”

Could Arteta land one more blockbuster summer signing?

Despite having arguably the Premier League’s strongest squad, the Spaniard says the club will always look to strengthen where possible.

3 Arteta has already secured the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes Credit: Getty

Arsenal are on the lookout for a left-sided attacker following Leandro Trossard's departure whilst Gabriel Martinelli's future hangs in the balance.



Liverpool target Bradley Barcola is a name that Arsenal have been linked with and Arteta let nothing slip when quizzed on his transfer plans.

“When we show ambition at the club it has to come from the very top and I think the ownership has been very supportive with everything we are doing at the club,” he said.

“The motivation is always there to be better. If we can identify the talent to make us better then we have to do it but we have to focus on what we have in house to make sure they evolve, grow and be better.

“You can see how crazy and unpredictable the league is. It's better not to talk too much, be prepared, be open and hopefully we can wrap up the transfer window in a really positive way.”

Sports.title: Frank Lampard reveals transfer chat with Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho before Coventry’s Premier League return
Sports.content:
Coventry City manager Frank Lampard has revealed he consulted Jose Mourinho over an undisclosed player earlier this summer.

The pair's relationship was thrust back into the spotlight this month with the release of 'Mourinho' - a three-part Netflix documentary about the Special One's storied career.

4 Lampard is back in the Premier League having masterfully guided Coventry to promotion Credit: Getty

4 Mourinho is surprisingly back at the Bernabeu after recent spells with Roma, Fenerbahce and Benfica Credit: Getty

Chelsea legend Lampard gives fascinating insight into the methods of his famous two-time boss at Stamford Bridge, who has now returned to Real Madrid for a second spell.

Lampard, meanwhile, is gearing up for the return of Championship winners Coventry to the Premier League after a 25-year absence.

He takes his Sky Blues to champions Arsenal for the 2026/27 season's curtain-raiser on Friday night - live on talkSPORT.

Joining us for an exclusive interview, Lampard's ex-England teammate Darren Bent jokingly asked whether he could potentially call in a favour with Mourinho and nab a few unwanted Galacticos this summer. Maybe Kylian Mbappe or Rodrygo?

"Yeah, I'm sure Doug [King - the Coventry owner] would love the wages. It would be triple or quadruple our wage bill!" Lampard responded.

"Jose's always there. Between us now, I did message him the other day about another player - not a Real Madrid player - but a player that he worked with previously and he's always on call.

"It takes him a couple of days sometimes. I know he's a busy man. But he came back with a very, very detailed talk about a certain player we're talking about.

"We've got that connection forever now - the Chelsea boys, Jose and that little group that you saw in the documentary - and those sort of bonds do stay forever."

What did Lampard learn from Mourinho?

One highly-publicised moment from the documentary was Lampard recalling a conversation with Mourinho in the shower during his early days with Chelsea in 2004.

The former England midfielder remembered Mourinho telling him he was already the best player in the world, but would only be recognised as such by winning trophies.

Lampard would go on to become Chelsea's all-time record goalscorer, winning every trophy available along the way.

Their relationship turning increasingly complicated through the years, starting with Lampard's unexpected release from Stamford Bridge under Mourinho's second tenure in 2014.

There was no love lost years later when Lampard took charge of Chelsea and Mourinho went to Tottenham.

But the Coventry boss admitted Mourinho's influence on his managerial career is undeniable - even if it looks a little different for him personally.

When asked what he learned from Mourinho and the other great managers since taking over at Derby for his first job in 2018, Lampard responded: "Lots.

"I've watched the doc and it was great memories, specifically the first one, because it was just a Chelsea story, and it just brought back so many great things.

4 Mourinho transformed Lampard into one of the greatest players in world football Credit: Getty

"I knew I loved Jose from a long time ago, but seeing it all back was great.

"I worked with lots of great managers. He specifically was the one that impacted my career the most, in the moment he came in, because of the confidence he gave me.

"I think many managers have tried to imitate Jose, to a degree, and I wouldn't or couldn't do that because I don't have his characteristics. I have my own.

"So there's little bits and snippets of things that he said and the personal impacts he had on me that I try to have by being close to my players and being able to communicate with them in the right way. I try and do it in my own way.

"I try and be close to the players so they feel like I'm a coach on the pitch, but if they've got problems off the pitch... because I felt like Jose was that for me.

"I'm trying to do management my own way. It's been eight years. It feels like it's flown by but what I've probably learned the most is to get my own balance right in terms of... you can't win every game.

4 Lampard has also come up against Mourinho as a manager on numerous occasions Credit: AFP

"You're gonna be tested in those ways. You can't search for perfection every day. You have to get your balance right off the pitch and on the pitch and prioritise the things that really matter.

"Hopefully these 18 months at Coventry, I've been able to show that that's a little personal improvement for me.

"And it actually makes my life easier to get that balance right, because you get your time to rest, it's a stressful job that will tax you, but you have to understand when you're in it, that's what it is."

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins open to Saudi transfer as Al Hilal prepare second offer for Aston Villa star
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins open to Saudi transfer as Al Hilal prepare second offer for Aston Villa star

Aston Villa are set to reject Al Hilal's opening bid of £38million to sign Ollie Watkins, talkSPORT understands.

The Aston Villa striker is open to a move to the Saudi Pro League outfit, who are expected to make an improved bid.



3 Watkins is open to joining Al Hilal Credit: Getty

If Watkins were to leave Villa Park, it would open the door for Unai Emery's side to reignite their interest in Nicolas Jackson.

However, talkSPORT understands Villa are reluctant to sell the England international.

talkSPORT revealed last month that discussions had taken place with Chelsea over signing the Senegal international.



Unai Emery previously worked with Jackson, who Chelsea value at £65million, during their time at Villarreal.

As for Watkins, he has less than two years remaining on his current Villa deal.



The 30-year-old joined the club from Brentford in 2020 and was part of the side which won the Europa League last season.

Watkins has scored 108 goals in 278 appearances across all competitions for Villa.



An exit from the club this summer would leave Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo as Emery's only senior centre-forwards.

Both players are currently fitness doubts for their season opener against Brighton on Sunday, though.

Al Hilal's striker search

Al Hilal have also held talks with Harry Kane over a potential move for the England captain. However, as previously revealed by talkSPORT, he is expected to stay at Bayern Munich.

3 Al Hilal have also held talks with Kane, but he is expected to stay at Bayern Credit: Getty



Former Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis is playing a key role in the pursuit of a new centre-forward.

It comes amid uncertainty surrounding Karim Benzema's future at the club.

The 38-year-old joined Al Hilal from Al Ittihad in February on a deal until the summer of 2027.

talkSPORT understands talks were held between Benzema and the club last month over his future.



He is believed to want a prominent role as opposed to a scenario which would see him only registered for Asian Champions League matches.

It's also understood Al Hilal could offload Darwin Nunez on loan to fellow Saudi Pro League club Diriyah this summer.

3 Watkins has less than two years remaining on his current Villa deal Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, Francis joined Al Hilal in a senior recruiting role at the start of July after leaving the Cherries.



Simone Inzaghi's side have already signed Crysenzio Summerville from West Ham United this summer.

The Netherlands winger completed a £68million move to the club last month.

Sports.title: Sunderland’s £25m transfer at risk of collapse as player fails medical
Sports.content:
Sunderland’s £25m transfer at risk of collapse as player fails medical

Toulouse defender Dayann Methalie's move to Sunderland is hanging in the balance, talkSPORT understands.

Methalie is returning to France after failing his medical ahead of a move to the Stadium of Light.



3 Sunderland's move for Methalie hangs in the balance after he failed his medical Credit: Getty

Methalie had been given permission to formalise his transfer by his current club.

However, additional medical tests are now required for the 20-year-old.

As a result, he has departed the North East to return to France before a final decision is made.



Sunderland had agreed a £24million fee plus a further £1.7million in add-ons for the left-back.

It would have seen Methalie become the Black Cats' second new addition of the summer.



Regis Le Bris' side have already completed the signing of right-back Thomas Meunier on a free transfer.

However, their hopes of adding a new left-back before the start of the season have now been dented.



Sunderland begin their campaign away to newly-promoted Ipswich Town on Saturday, with kick-off at 3pm.

The Black Cats finished seventh on their return to the top-flight after nine years away last term.

As a result, they will compete in the Europa League this season, their first taste of European action since 1973.

3 Le Bris has made just one new signing ahead of Sunderland's season opener this weekend Credit: Getty



Who is Dayann Methalie?

Prospective new signing Methalie has already represented France up to Under-21 level.

He has scored twice in four caps for them since making his debut at that age group in October.

The Toulouse academy graduate featured 30 times for the club across all competitions last season.

Those appearances included 27 in Ligue 1 as they ended the campaign in ninth place.



Last term saw Methalie deployed as a left-wing-back for Toulouse, whilst he can also play as a central defender.

The potential collapse of his move to Sunderland comes after he was left out of the squad for his current club's latest fixture.

3 Methalie will return to France for additional medical tests after a £25m deal was agreed Credit: Alamy

Methalie was not involved alongside his teammates for their 2-1 friendly defeat to Hamburg on Saturday.



He could now feature in their season opener at home to Lyon this weekend, though.

The young defender missed six matches through injury last term.

His absence from the side in January followed a knee problem picked up at the start of the year.

Sports.title: Man City charges verdict update as Premier League chief admits frustration is ‘understandable’
Sports.content:
Premier League chief executive Richard Masters understands fan frustration over Manchester City's Financial Fair Play (FFP) charges.

The club are awaiting the verdict of a hearing into 130 alleged breaches of the league's FFP rules.

3 Premier League chief executive Masters has provided an update on City's 130 FFP charges Credit: Getty

City were charged with an initial 115 breaches by the Premier League back in February 2023.

The alleged offences are said to have taken place over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

An additional 15 charges were later added to take the total number to 130.

Although a hearing took place between September and December 2024, a verdict has yet to be reached.

Man City charges update

Masters has now provided an update ahead of the start of the new season.

The 2026/27 campaign begins on Friday, with Arsenal hosting Coventry City at 8pm, live on talkSPORT.

Prior to the new season, Masters spoke to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook at the Premier League's launch event on Tuesday.

Asked if a verdict is any closer to being announced, he admitted: "As every day elapses, we must be a day nearer.

"I obviously can't comment on it. I do understand the frustration. It has taken longer than expected, but we have to follow the process."

As for whether the wait, which has now reached 20 months, is damaging the top-flight, Masters added: "I hope not.

3 City are awaiting the verdict of a hearing into their charges, which concluded in December 2024 Credit: PA

"In the end, the Premier League's responsibility is to ask the Independent Commission to look at serious allegations and to establish the truth.

"That shouldn't be qualified by it taking too long, for example."

Premier League financial rule changes

The new season will also bring a change to the Premier League's financial rules.

As of this term, profit and sustainability rules (PSR) will be replaced by squad cost ratio (SCR).

It represents the adoption of a system similar to that already implemented by UEFA.

SCR limits clubs' spending on players to a percentage of their football-related revenue.

3 Masters is hopeful the new squad cost ratio rules will improve the Premier League Credit: Getty

That figure has been set at 85 per cent by the Premier League, compared to 70 per cent in UEFA competitions.

Asked how the change will improve the league and helps those sides lower down the food chain, Masters explained: "I’m not sure.

"It took us two years to get that in. That was a very long consultation about PSR and what should come forward.

"Obviously one of the motivations behind bringing in squad cost ratio is to have close alignment with UEFA.

"Ours is a slightly different system. They’re at 70 per cent, we’re a more generous 85 per cent and that was the same with PSR.

"Our limits have always been set higher than UEFA’s, more flexibility for clubs to invest over time to allow the chasing pack to compete.

"Squad cost ratio is designed to do the same. So I think we’ve got a very good competitive balance in the Premier League and I hope the SCR reinforces that."

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala confirms medical condition diagnosis after collapsing on pitch for second time
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala confirms medical condition diagnosis after collapsing on pitch for second time

Jamal Musiala has been diagnosed with temporary episodes of absence caused by neurological dysfunction after collapsing for the second time in a week.

The Bayern Munich midfielder went down off the ball in Tuesday’s 4-2 friendly victory over Heidenheim.



5 Players from both sides swarmed around Musiala after he collapsed Credit: Getty

5 Musiala looked unsteady on his feet as he was subsequently helped off the pitch Credit: Getty

Musiala had only been on the pitch for six minutes when the incident occurred.

His fall quickly sparked alarm with Bayern’s medical team quickly rushing to the player’s aid.



Musiala’s teammates crowded around the 23-year-old as he received treatment.

The Germany international was able to rise to his feet and walk off the pitch, even breaking out into a brief jog before being substituted.



It comes just three days after Musiala collapsed during Bayern's 3-1 win over RB Leipzig on Saturday.

He missed the team presentation on Monday after an individual training session.



Therefore his involvement against Heidenheim so soon after Saturday's collapse could be viewed as a surprise.

The latest incident will undoubtedly raise concerns over the player’s health ahead of this weekend’s German Super Cup clash against Borussia Dortmund.

Musiala opens up on his health diagnosis

Following the match, Musiala took to Instagram to reassure fans his condition won't have any lasting effects on his health and career once treated.

"First things first - I’m doing well! Above all, I’m incredibly grateful for all your messages and your support!," he wrote.



5 Harry Kane nervously looked on as teammate Musiala slowly rose to his feet after collapsing Credit: Getty

"I understand that many of you are worried. I want to put those concerns to rest today and explain a little more: I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary episodes of absence that are easily treatable and are caused by a neurological dysfunction.

"These can lead to the moments that have occurred recently, such as against Leipzig and now in Heidenheim.

"I know that they may seem scary at first glance - but for me, they are currently simply part of my everyday life.



"I am receiving the best possible medical care in this regard, and I am very optimistic. FC Bayern and the people closest to me are always by my side and supporting me on this journey."

He continued: "What is important is that there is no additional health risk beyond this. In close consultation and regular communication with the specialists, it was my personal wish to face this challenge and, with the approval of the neurological specialists, to continue doing what helps me most in my recovery: simply living my everyday life and continuing to pursue my passion of playing football.

"I have taken responsibility for that decision. Overall, I have a very good feeling and I am on a good path.

5 Musiala was thankfully able to get back on his feet quickly Credit: Getty



"What helps me most along the way is continuing to chase victories and titles with my team, with your incredible support. I hope this helps you understand me better.

"At the same time, I ask for your understanding that I would like to continue keeping this matter within the circle of my closest confidants, the club and the experts."

Bayern complete their pre-season preparations in style

Vincent Kompany's side continued their impressive pre-season form in Tuesday's 4-2 win.

Goals from Filipe Chavez and Arijon Ibrahimovic drew Bayern level before Kompany's side showed their superiority.



Luis Diaz and summer signing Nathaniel Brown added two late goals to see off their opponents.

The win sets Bayern up perfectly for Saturday's first shot at silverware against their Der Klassiker rivals Dortmund.

5 Vincent Kompany says he is ready to win it all at Bayern this season Credit: Getty

After that, Bayern launch their Bundesliga campaign against VfB Stuttgart on Friday, August 28 as they search for a third consecutive title.



Assessing his side's goals ahead of the new season, Kompany was clear in terms of his expectations.

“The goals with FC Bayern are always the highest - winning the Bundesliga, winning the Pokal (German Cup) winning the Champions League and maybe even winning every game.

"We’ll definitely be trying to achieve that.”

Sports.title: Man found dead at Charlton’s home stadium, The Valley, as statement given
Sports.content:
Man found dead at Charlton’s home stadium, The Valley, as statement given

A man has been found dead at the stadium of Championship club Charlton Athletic.

Police are investigating after a body was discovered at The Valley on Tuesday morning.

3 The news was confirmed by Charlton on Tuesday evening Credit: Getty

Officers were called to the ground following an incident in the early hours of the morning with a man being pronounced dead at the scene.

Charlton statement

In a statement, Charlton said: "Charlton Athletic are supporting the police with their enquiries following the discovery of a deceased individual at The Valley on Tuesday morning.

"Police were called to the stadium today after an incident that occurred in the early hours of Monday morning. A male was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

"The death remains under investigation. Anyone with information, or who may have witnessed the incident, is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference 2809/18AUG.

"Everyone at Charlton Athletic would like to express their deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the individual's family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

"The club are continuing to assist the authorities with their enquiries and respectfully ask that the privacy of those affected is respected.

"There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of the club. Charlton Athletic would also like to thank its staff for the professionalism they have shown while dealing with a particularly difficult and distressing situation."

Earlier on Tuesday, Charlton had announced a match involving their Under-21 side had been relocated from The Valley.

They had been due to face Bolton Wanderers in the U21 Professional Development League.

However, the fixture was subsequently moved to the Addicks' training ground at Sparrows Lane.

3 Charlton confirmed they were supporting police with their enquiries Credit: Getty

In a statement confirming the move, the club said: "Due to unforeseen circumstances, Charlton’s U21 Professional Development League fixture against Bolton Wanderers on Tuesday afternoon has been relocated from The Valley to Sparrows Lane."

The statement added: "The club would like to apologies for any inconvenience caused to supporters planning to attend the fixture."

Bolton won the match 1-0, with Toby Ritchie scoring the game's only goal.

Charlton began the new Championship season with a home match at The Valley on Saturday.

Nathan Jones' side came from behind to beat Derby County thanks to goals from Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell.

Their next home fixture is currently scheduled for Saturday, August 29.

3 An Under-21 fixture was relocated from The Valley on Tuesday afternoon amid police enquiries Credit: Getty

The Addicks will face Preston North End following trips to take on West Ham United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Those fixtures take place in the league and Carabao Cup, respectively.

Sports.title: Arsenal CEO waiting for ‘right opportunity’ in transfer market as Myles Lewis-Skelly future addressed
Sports.content:
Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick has confirmed the club remain open to the idea of further incomings this summer.

The Premier League champions have spent almost £150m during the transfer window with the acquisitions of Bruno Guimaraes, Piero Hincapie, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier.

5 Arsenal's £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes is is one of the most high-profile signings of the summer Credit: Getty

With an almost complete squad to choose from, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta remains hopeful of adding further firepower to the left side of his attack.

Tzolis was brought in to replace the recently departed Leandro Trossard, while doubts remain over the future of Gabriel Martinelli.

Arsenal hold a long-standing interest in Paris Saint-Germain’s wantaway winger Bradley Barcola.

Liverpool remain frontrunners to sign the France international but with Arsenal still in the market for additional signings, could they hijack the Reds’ move for the star?

Arsenal CEO leaves the door ajar for new signings

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT on Tuesday about potential further transfer activity, Garlick said: “We are always looking to improve our squad.

“As I say, we're not going to sit here and say job done. We'll always be looking to see what options we've got to improve the squad.

“There's still a couple of weeks left in the window to go so if the right opportunity comes up then we will explore that.

“And as I say we're always looking to add to the squad and bring in quality players. Obviously where we are now as Premier League champions it's always difficult to find players that are going to improve you.

“So it's maybe a bit of a smaller market, but if that opportunity arises then we'll look to take it.”

Asked if the club needs a player clear-out ahead of the new season, Garlick said: “I think I said right at the start of the season, most clubs now embark on player trading.

5 Could the Gunners launch a late bid for Bradley Barcola under the noses of Liverpool? Credit: Getty

5 Arteta is hoping to complete one more deal before closing the door on incomings Credit: Getty

“The models that most clubs have involve players coming in and going out. We do have a big squad.

“We've obviously seen a couple of players going in Christian [Norgaard] and Trossard but obviously we will look at what's best for our squad.

“We're always looking to improve the squad so if that means some players may leave and other players come in then we'll look at that.

“But I think player trading is now just a natural part of the game.”

What is the latest on Myles Lewis-Skelly's future?

Garlick was asked about the future of Myles Lewis-Skelly who has been linked with a move away from the Emirates Stadium this summer having been offered to rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The academy graduate has been active during pre-season and starred in the Gunners’ comfortable Community Shield victory over Manchester City on Sunday.

5 Myles Lewis-Skelly has impressed in pre-seasosn despite speculation over his future Credit: Getty

The 19-year-old has attracted plenty of plaudits of late including from ex-England captain Wayne Rooney who urged his former club Manchester United to secure his services.

But Garlick has heaped praise on the versatile star as he claimed the club want to keep hold of their best players.

“Myles has had a fantastic end to last season and he started this season really well and as I say we're always looking to retain and build on our best players,” he said.

“Obviously there may be speculation, I'm not going to go into that from other clubs but we're very happy with Myles and the position he's in at the club.”

Another player linked with a move away from the club this summer is Gabriel Martinelli who recently turned down a move to Galatasaray.

The Brazilian could still end his adventure with the Premier League champions before the end of the transfer window after seven years at the club and Garlick admits seeing players depart is always difficult to endure.

5 Martinelli is set for a move this summer after being left out of the Community Shield squad Credit: Getty

“It’s hard,” Garlick said. “Obviously you make relationships with players and the players have played their part, every one of them in the success we've had over the last couple of years.

“I think that as I say players coming and going is just a natural part of football so I don't think any player ever thinks that they're necessarily going to be at a club forever.

“But as I say from our point of view we're very respectful of players that may want to leave and players that are looking for more time to play. so we'll continue to build on the squad and as I say player training is part of that.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace land £11m American star, Sunderland's move for £25.7m new boy is in danger after medical... and Rodri sends emotional message to Man City fans: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa to reject Al Hilal's £38m Watkins bid - as Ajax hold talks over Bailey

Aston Villa will reject Al Hilal's bid for striker Ollie Watkins. The Saudi club made an offer worth £38million for the England striker to test Villa's resolve.

Watkins, 30, is open to the move as the Saudi side have made a couple of proposals this summer but Villa want to keep him.

Ajax, meanwhile, have held initial talks over a move for Villa’s Leon Bailey.

Tyjon wants out as Arsenal hover

Blackburn Rovers prospect Igor Tyjon has asked to leave amid ongoing interest from Arsenal. The 18-year-old forward has represented both England and Poland at youth level.

Ipswich's £18m bid rejected

Ipswich Town have had an offer of around £18m rejected by Bayer Leverkusen for Argentina midfielder Exequiel Palacios.

Exequiel Palacios featured for Argentina at the World Cup

Brighton bag Promise

Brighton have signed Canada striker Promise David, 25, from Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise on a season's loan with obligation to buy for £22m.

American boy joins Palace
