R. Una cosa que aprendí en los barcos es que una decisión tomada no es una decisión acabada; puedes ir reconduciendo si ves que no aparece la boya que esperabas.

P. Eso es la ley de amnistía, ¿no?

R. ¡Qué lío se montó con eso! Y qué cosas terribles dijeron algunos. Ahora parece que no dijeron nada. Hubo gente que hasta se manifestó antes de que la ley saliera. Y ahora resulta que Europa dice que está ok.

P. ¿La política necesita fontaneros o fontaneras?

R. La política necesita gente capaz y honrada para dedicarse al servicio público.

P. ¿Qué pensó la primera vez que oyó hablar de Leire Díez?

R. No voy a entrar en eso. No merece la pena.

P. ¿La conoce?

R. Creo que no la vi nunca.

P. ¿Alguna vez a lo largo de su carrera política ha recurrido a un perfil parecido?

R. Toda la gente que yo tengo de concejal es gente capaz y a los hechos me remito: arrasamos.

Abel Caballero, alcalde de Vigo, en su despacho del Ayuntamiento el pasado 16 de julio. Adrian Irago

P. ¿A qué artistas les tiene ganas? ¿Para quién le gustaría calentar el escenario?

R. A Coldplay. Y vendrán.

P. ¿Y Bad Bunny? ¿Si viene, le hará una casiña?

R. No descarto que venga. Y le hacemos una casiña enseguida. La que hizo él no estaba mal, pero la que le haríamos aquí sería mucho mejor.

P. ¿Y por qué le gusta salir al escenario?

R. Yo saludo a todos los artistas. Subirse a un escenario delante de 50.000 o 100.000 personas es emocionante. Nosotros damos 15 conciertos y yo presento los 15. Luego hay muchas fiestas en los barrios y yo hablo en todas.

P. Hace unos años se quejaron algunos vecinos de los villancicos que salen de las farolas, que una cosa es la Navidad y otra, Guantánamo. ¿Arreglaron?

R. Era la hermana de una candidata del PP. La ciudad es consciente de que la Navidad nos puso en el mundo porque los países conectan en directo cuando yo aprieto el botón de las luces. Y toda España. No es fácil hacer una cosa así. ¿Quién presenta denuncias en los juzgados? El PP y el Bloque [Nacionalista Galego], que quieren apagar la Navidad. Pero perdieron todas. Es cierto que la Navidad puede tener un efecto no deseado, algunas molestias, como en todas las fiestas del mundo, pero la ciudad adora la Navidad. Si fuera de otra forma, algo me dirían por la calle, ¿no?

P. Dicen que aquí la Navidad empieza en verano. ¿Dónde la guardan?

R. En la nube porque somos modernos [ríe]. La empezamos a bajar a finales de julio. Iluminamos 480 calles. ¿Y qué dice la gente? “Alcalde, mi calle no tiene luces”. Exactamente lo contrario de lo que el PP y el Bloque, y Rueda y Feijóo dicen.

P. ¿Tiene sorpresas para la de este año? Piense que le toca sorprender a un nuevo alcalde de Nueva York.

R. Mamdani es un gran alcalde. Yo espero que este año conozca que Vigo tiene la mejor Navidad de este planeta. El año que viene le haré una sorpresa y al siguiente, que es su año de elecciones, lo invitaré a que venga. Y vendrá, porque todos los que invité y no vinieron perdieron las elecciones.

P. ¿Qué ha supuesto en términos de ingresos para la ciudad esta revolución de las luces de Navidad?

R. El retorno son 800 millones de euros. ¿Cuánto nos cuesta? Tres. Y se generan miles de empleos, pero además hay algo imposible de medir: el nombre. Vigo es la Navidad del mundo: está en Nueva York, en Londres, en París, en Roma, en todas partes. Eso es marca ciudad y es imposible calcular el valor. Es infinito eso.

P. ¿Se imaginaba hasta dónde iba a llegar todo este fenómeno?

R. No. Que cuando suene la palabra Navidad piensen en Vigo era imposible de pensar. Todo el mundo quiere ser Vigo. Nosotros no pagamos anuncios de Navidad. El anuncio soy yo. Ahora en las agencias de viajes hay anuncios de viajes a la Navidad de Vigo.

P. ¿Y qué le hace más ilusión: la Navidad o ser sede del Mundial?

R. La Navidad ya está. Ser sede del Mundial me hace mucha ilusión, pero la Xunta y la Diputación dicen que no pagan las obras. Las dos del Partido Popular. Verán lo que hacen.

P. ¿Cómo cree que terminará eso?

R. Seremos sede del Mundial.

P. ¿Tiene otros talentos ocultos además del break dance?

R. Yo no tengo ningún talento. A mí me apetece ir en una bici BMX y este año lo voy a hacer. ¿Por qué no lo voy a hacer? ¿Porque tengo 80 años? Pues sí que puedo. Este año me subo a una BMX y el que viene haré skate. Hay que probar las cosas. Y cuando veo que alguien está celebrando un cumpleaños, me acerco y les canto el cumpleaños feliz y además, me gusta hacerlo en inglés, que es muy celebrado por el personal.

P. ¡Como Marilyn Monroe!

R. Bueno, Marilyn lo hizo de otra forma, especial. Yo canto mal, toco la guitarra mal, pero la toco igual. Tenemos que perder algunos complejos. Eso lo aprendí a lo largo de la vida. Yo hago las cosas porque me apetece hacerlas.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Por Mónaco sin datos en el móvil ni wifi, la mejor manera de recorrer el Principado
World.content:
Del Casino de Montecarlo a la catedral, pasando por Le Rocher y el Palacio Principesco, esta pequeña ciudad-estado hay que pasearla sin distracciones

En mis artículos para El Viajero no suelo usar la primera persona. Sin embargo, en esta ocasión procede hacerlo, no tanto como aviso para navegantes, sino para que se entienda mejor lo narrado.

A lo largo de los últimos años he visitado en más de una ocasión el Principado de Mónaco, al que es muy fácil llegar con el tren que bordea la Costa Azul, hallándose, por ejemplo, a menos de media hora de Niza. Mi primera vez en la patria de Raniero y Grace Kelly vino precedida de un vendaval de optimismo. Recordaba consejos de profesores del pasado, bien felices de narrar al alumnado cómo esta ciudad-estado consta de unos dos kilómetros cuadrados de superficie total, lo que hace suponer un fácil dominio de ese espacio, poblado por poco más de 38.000 habitantes, de los cuales 9.600 son de nacionalidad monegasca.

Más información Viaje por la Polonia judía

Bien es sabido que las apariencias engañan. Mónaco, independizado de Génova desde 1297, no forma parte de la Unión Europea pese a sus contactos más que frecuentes con Francia e Italia. Este factor, a priori, no supone ningún problema, o al menos antes no preocupaba a ningún visitante por el hábito de ir, a lo sumo, con un mapa para orientarse por sus calles. Pero los tiempos han cambiado y ahora mismo para muchos turistas resulta imprescindible disponer de internet para caminar con garantías. En mi caso confieso que suelo usar los mapas digitales como brújula base, para, a continuación, prescindir del móvil y así poder mirar bien aquello que piso sin condenarme a la pantalla.

El problema es que en Mónaco no puedes ir tan suelto —el roaming gratuito de la UE no se aplica de forma automática por ley—, al menos si es tu primera vez en el Principado, donde un exceso de confianza puede costarte una gran frustración, como fue mi caso tras bajar del tren, sentirme satisfecho por alcanzar el Casino de Montecarlo, que es el nombre de uno de los cuatro barrios del centro de Mónaco pese a confundirse por todo el conjunto, y luego soltarme hasta, literalmente, perderme en una serie de avenidas sin ninguna referencia visual válida para rehacer el camino y recuperar la cordura del itinerario.

Lo más grotesco de esa experiencia fue que pude entender con rotundidad mi fracaso al subir una cuesta e informarme un cartel de estar en Beausoleil, pueblo francés que junto a Montecarlo forma una sola aglomeración urbana. A partir de ese punto respiré hondo gracias a las vistas, perfectas para situarme y pasear sin necesidad de datos ni de conexión wifi al comprender la morfología de la ciudad.

Exterior del casino de Montecarlo. David Gee (Alamy / Cordon Press)

La clave de todo estriba, sobre todo para caminar sin riesgo a extraviarse, en salir de la estación por el sitio justo, que siempre es la Rue Grimaldi, e ir hasta la Avenue d’Ostende, desde la que cualquier ruta es fácil, si bien recomiendo ascenderla e ir hacia el Casino de Montecarlo porque siempre es el mejor punto de partida al ser un icono alejado del resto que sirve como Kilómetro cero hacia los demás.

Mónaco legalizó el juego en 1854 y necesitaba un edificio de postín para atraer a buscadores de fortuna que quisieran combinar la osadía con el prestigio de ganar dinero en un marco de veras incomparable, como lo fue el casino desde 1878, cuando Charles Garnier, autor de la Ópera de París, le confirió su actual aspecto. Este templo mundial de la apuesta, inmortalizado por Stefan Zweig en la novela 24 horas en la vida de una mujer (1924), ha proporcionado ingentes dividendos a la familia Grimaldi, si bien en nuestro siglo su facturación no es decisiva para las finanzas del Principado.

Desde el casino, con una plaza dispuesta para transitar entre el lujo y la egolatría contemporánea del selfi, lo mejor es volver a la Avenue d’Ostende, parándonos en cualquiera de sus pequeños miradores para aprehender mejor por dónde nos movemos sin marearnos por la enorme densidad de edificios entre imposibles rascacielos y hoteles de la Belle Époque afeados por estos excesos constructivos. Al final la vista se habitúa a los mismos porque cada sitio tiene su propia belleza, aunque aquí siempre es más hermoso mirar a la izquierda para admirar el Puerto de Hércules del barrio de La Condamine, que rodearemos para llegar al otro espectáculo que la vista nos ofrece en esta panorámica: Le Rocher, o la roca en las alturas donde se concentran los distintos poderes monegascos.

Vista de Le Rocher, donde se concentran los distintos poderes monegascos. Westend61 (getty images)

La encrucijada hacia esta meta se ubica, valga la redundancia, en el cruce de la Avenue d’Ostende con su paralela dedicada a John Fitzgerald Kennedy, que da paso al Quai dedicado a Alberto I, con comienzo y final capitalizado por dos estatuas que honran a leyendas del automovilismo. La primera es de William Grover, mientras la segunda, ya en las estribaciones de las escaleras hacia Le Rocher, es un homenaje al campeonísimo argentino de la especialidad Juan Manuel Fangio, quien cosechó dos victorias en el Gran Premio más famoso del circo de la F1.

Monumento en recuerdo del piloto argentino de Juan Manuel Fangio, en Mónaco. Paul Quayle (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Desde esta estatua, una de las más fotografiadas de nuestro recorrido, disponemos de un pequeño abanico de opciones para escalar hacia la roca, aunque mi consejo es ir por las avenidas du Port y de la Porte Neuve para no repetir nuestros pasos y no aburrirnos cuando regresemos de esta expedición, que tiene como cumbre el Palacio Principesco en su homónima plaza, donde cada día, a las 11.55 en punto, se produce el muy vitoreado cambio de guardia de los Carabineros del Príncipe.

El Palacio Principesco, ubicado en la plaza homónima.

La primera piedra de la residencia real se puso a finales del siglo XIII, remodelándose hasta finales de la decimonovena centuria, cuando aún se rodeaba de una rica vegetación en los alrededores, poco a poco rebajada sin desaparecer del todo pese al crecimiento de estos aledaños, que en nuestra época mezclan lo esencial de cualquier centro urbano con un apabullante número de tiendas dedicadas a vender baratijas y souvenirs. Lo mejor, como sospecharán, es parar poquito en esos negocios y, aquí sí, caracolear por las callecitas sin temor a descarriarse porque todo queda cerca, de los miradores a la catedral, construida en 1875 y firmada por el arquitecto Charles Lenormand, con una blanquísima fachada que oculta un rico interior dividido en tres naves, a rebosar de obras de arte, muchas de ellas provenientes del anterior templo, demolido como preludio a su completa renovación de estilo neorromántico.

La catedral de Nuestra Señora Inmaculada, conocida también como catedral de Mónaco. Barry Winiker (getty images)

De la catedral —lugar de entierro del príncipe Rainiero III y la princesa Grace— al último hito de este pequeñísimo país median menos de 300 metros. Se trata del Museo Oceanográfico, impulsado por el príncipe Alberto I, cuya fama de gran navegante se simboliza por este legado, abierto al público en marzo de 1910 y dirigido a partir de 1957 (y durante más de 30 años), en coincidencia con el auge turístico, por el comandante Jacques-Yves Cousteau, fundamental para armar el aparato pedagógico de la institución, muy en consonancia con el transmitido en sus documentales televisivos que tanta popularidad le dieron durante la segunda mitad del siglo pasado.

Mónaco no encierra muchas dificultades para el visitante y puede saborearse al detalle en pocas horas con la virtud añadida de conseguir que muchos se sientan menos dependientes de la tecnología por esa carambola de no poder usar los datos del móvil como en la Unión Europea. Ahora que terminamos les confesaré que claro, seguro encuentran alguna red wifi disponible brindada por las autoridades, pero créanme, si prescinden de teclear su contraseña ganarán tiempo y el privilegio de poder andar con el cuerpo bien erguido y los ojos fijos en el horizonte, algo que, por desgracia, cada vez es menos habitual en cualquier latitud del planeta.

World.title: “Exceptional” 17th-century sketchbook donated to Rijksmuseum
World.content:
A 17th-century sketchbook containing 30 drawings has been hailed as a rare find after it was donated to the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

Several of the sketches have been attributed to the Frisian painter Rombould Uylenburgh, who was a well-known artist in his day but fell into obscurity following his death in 1627 or 1628.

The book is known as the Van Eeghen sketchbook, after the family of Amsterdam merchants who owned it for three centuries. The sketches, some of which were made on blue paper, have retained their colour because the book has not been on display.

The Rijksmuseum said it was unusual for an artist’s sketchbook from the 17th century to survive intact for so long. More commonly, the drawings are torn out and sold individually, or lost.

Only two sketches and a handful of paintings by Uylenburgh were thought to have survived when the sketchbook resurfaced in 1935.

The drawings in the book were only attributed to him in 2013, after the owner saw they were similar to one of the artist’s works in the Rijksmuseum’s collection.

Uylenburgh was born in Friesland in 1580 but spent most of his life in Poland after his family emigrated to Krakow. He because the court painter of King Sigismund III Vasa and went on to build a successful career in the port city of Danzig.

His brother, Hendrik, returned to the Dutch Republic and based himself in Amsterdam. By 1625 had established himself as Rembrandt’s main art dealer and is believed to have introduced the painter to his cousin, Saskia van Uylenburgh, who married Rembrandt in 1633.

The Van Eeghen sketchbook is the focus of a display in the museum from August 19 until November 29.

World.title: Holidaymakers warned not to bring home “destructive” beetle
World.content:
The Dutch food standards watchdog NVWA has urged returning holidaymakers not to bring back foreign invaders after a Japanese beetle was found in a freight shipment from Italy.

The insect was found dead in a plastic container that was being transported from a region of Italy where Japanese beetles are known to live.

The NVWA set traps in the container to see if any live beetles had crept inside, but none were found. But the agency told people coming back from southern Europe and transport companies to be alert and report any specimens they found.

“The NVWA is explicitly asking trading and logistics companies to be alert for beetles hitching a lift when they travel to or through the named areas,” the agency said in a statement.

“Do not in any event leave the doors and windows of your vehicle open for longer than necessary and try to check goods and packing for beetles before departure if possible.“

Japanese beetles are not considered a pest in their native country, where their numbers are controlled by natural predators.

But in recent years they have been spotted in Italy, Croatia, Switzerland, Germany and the Azores. The German province of Hessen is the closest area to the Netherlands with an established population.

They are regarded as highly destructive because they feed on a wide range of vegetation. Adult beetles will devour leaves and stems of plants, while their larvae eat grass roots and weeds.

The NVWA has also published advice on its website advising people how to tell Japanese beetles apart from similar looking native species.

World.title: Inflation making plant-based foods cheaper than meat and dairy
World.content:
Plant-based foods now cost less than meat and dairy equivalents at nine major supermarkets in the Netherlands, according to new research published by food organisation ProVeg.

“It’s remarkable that this is happening,” Martine van Haperen, nutrition and health expert at ProVeg, told DutchNews.

“It’s normally been very difficult for plant-based products to compete with animal-based ones. What we’re seeing now is that store brands like Albert Heijn have expanded their own-brand products, making them more affordable.”

The bigger driver, she said, is inflation. “Inflation has hit animal products much harder than plant-based ones, and that is because animal products require much more resources to be produced.”

Cheaper across the board

ProVeg, which has tracked the price gap since 2022, compared the cheapest plant-based version of each product with the cheapest animal one, priced per kilo, at nine chains in late April.

A basic basket of six items stocked everywhere – mince, burgers, butter, milk, yoghurt and cheese – was cheaper in its plant-based form at every chain, by around 18% on average.

Shoppers buying staples such as mince and milk can save up to 30%, the organisation said, with the widest gaps at Plus and Dirk and the narrowest at the organic chain Ekoplaza. Plant-based butter came in 48% cheaper.

The plant-based versions of some products remain far more expensive, however: mayonnaise costs almost four times as much as the animal version, while vegan yoghurt and kwark are both more than double the price.

The bigger basket

ProVeg also compared a wider basket of 14 products – adding items such as sausages, shoarma and mayonnaise that not every chain sells in a plant-based version. On that fuller list the plant-based basket costs more at four shops: Dirk, Hoogvliet, Jumbo and Picnic. At Albert Heijn the two come out level.

Dirk is the odd one out, with its plant-based basics are among the cheapest of any chain, but its wider basket ends up 25% more expensive than the meat one. It stocks a plant-based version in all 14 categories – just not a cheap own-brand in every one, and those pricier extras drag the total up.

World.title: Police get stop and search powers after shootings in Zuidoost
World.content:
Police will be able to stop and search anyone for weapons in part of Amsterdam-Zuidoost for a week from Thursday, after a long series of shooting and gun threats that the city says often involve minors.

The mayor, police and public prosecutor have designated the H-buurt, the K-buurt and the Nelson Mandelapark a security risk area until August 27. Inside it, police can search people without having any specific cause for suspicion.

Authorities recorded 18 firearm-related incidents in the area between June 1 and August 1, ranging from threats made at gunpoint to shootings that left people wounded.

In one case on August 3, a shot fired during a confrontation passed through a wall into a child’s bedroom. A minor was inside the house at the time, reported local broadcaster AT5.

Second summer running

It is the second summer in a row that Zuidoost has faced such a regime. Last year’s designation followed the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old and was extended into September.

Extra police patrols had already been deployed this summer, the city said, but had not been enough to restore calm.

Controversial tactics

Preventive searching has been used in Rotterdam for a long time. It was introduced there in 2002 and now covers large parts of Rotterdam-Zuid.

The tactic is controversial, with opposition and coalition parties on Rotterdam’s council having accused the city of ethnic profiling. Stop and searches in Rotterdam require at least three police officers at every search to guard against it.

Amsterdam dropped preventive searching in 2015, deeming it ineffective. The city has still used it repeatedly over the past year, in the red light district, over New Year and now twice in Zuidoost.

World.title: Budget talks offer no clear route to majority for Dutch cabinet
World.content:
The cabinet has begun talks with opposition parties to try to secure a majority for next month’s annual budget, with prime minister Rob Jetten setting a target of August 28 to secure a deal.

The three-party coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house and holds less than one-third of the seats in the Senate.

Commentators say the choice boils down to two options: either do a deal with the main left-wing party Progressief Nederland (PRO) – which was formed by the merger of PvdA and GroenLinks – or try to forge a majority on the right with JA21. But neither route is straightforward.

PRO leader Jesse Klaver told NRC this week that he supported the cabinet’s plans to invest €2.1 billion extra in defence and €1 billion in education.

But his party wants to force the cabinet to scrap its proposed €6.5 billion cuts to social security and raise the money instead through higher taxes on wealth and corporations.

Klaver said he was prepared to drive a hard bargain on the welfare cuts even though they are not due to be introduced until next year’s budget. His stance is backed up by the trade union movement, which has called a national transport workers’ strike for September 9 to protest against the reforms.

“We won’t let people live with uncertainty about cuts in the future,” Klaver said. “These need to be taken off the table this autumn.

VVD reluctance

The right-wing liberal VVD says the cuts are non-negotiable because they are not prepared to increase borrowing or let the budget deficit exceed the European Union’s 3% limit.

The VVD has been reluctant to negotiate with PRO, which it explicitly ruled out as a coalition partner during last year’s general election campaign and in the negotiations to form the current cabinet at the start of this year.

But the path to a majority on the right is even more complicated. Support from PRO would give the cabinet a healthy majority in the lower house and a near majority in the Senate, where the government needs to find just two more votes from smaller parties.

JA21 has nine seats in the lower house – one fewer than the number needed for a majority – but only two senators. The party wants the cabinet to cut welfare even further and reduce taxes, including the so-called “freedom contribution” proposed by the Christian Democrats (CDA) to fund defence spending.

JA21: “Constructive”

Its leader, Joost Eerdmans, said a video call with Jetten and the two deputy prime ministers, Dilan Yesilgöz of the VVD and Bart van den Brink of the CDA, had been “good and constructive” and further discussions would follow, without disclosing further details.

Geert Wilders’ far-right PVV group and the even more extreme Forum voor Democratie (FVD), which have 25 seats between them, are refusing to lend the cabinet any support.

DNA, the splinter group of former PVV MPs led by Gidi Markuszower, is willing to co-operate with the cabinet, but has not been invited to the negotiating table.

Markuszower has warned he will demand a high price for his party’s support: “People at home are crying out for more money in their pocket, lower costs, more houses, more secuity and less asylum, but the cabinet is failing on all fronts.”

BBB shut out

The farmers’ party BBB has also been left off the guest list for this week’s talks, even though the party has 11 seats in the Senate.

The BBB has been unhappy with the government’s plans to impose more limits on the agriculture sector in order to cut nitrogen pollution, which has triggered a new wave of farmers’ protests over the summer.

The party has been riven by defections in both houses in the last year, particularly the upper house, where five BBB senators have left the party, including two who switched allegiance to its arch-nemesis, the progressive liberal party D66.

Heinen absent

Even more intriguing is the fact that finance minister Eelco Heinen, who will present the budget when parliament reconvenes on September 15, is not attending the first two days of negotiations.

Heinen excused himself on the basis that the focus of the talks was to secure “political commitment” rather than discuss the details of fiscal policy, but Klaver remarked: “I can’t remember a previous time when the finance minister wasn’t there for the budget process.”

The Christian parties ChristenUnie and SGP, as well as the pensioners’ party 50Plus, are also due to meet with ministers on Wednesday.

World.title: Water board call in police after drought inspectors face threats
World.content:
Water authorities in Noord-Brabant have contacted police after inspectors received threats for checking whether local residents were breaking drought restrictions.

The Brabantse Delta water board, which covers an area centred on Breda stretching from the Maas to the Belgian border, has imposed a ban on taking water from streams and ditches between 9am and 9pm.

Inspectors have been using drones equipped with cameras to monitor fields since the ban was introduced a month ago. But staff who were named in a recent article on news website Omroep Brabant about their work have since ben subjected to threats.

Water board chairman Joris Bengevoord would not go into detail about the threats, but said a criminal complaint had been filed with police so they could investigate.

“It’s very serious and goes way too far,” he told NOS. “It’s not OK that they’re being threatened, which is why I’m speaking out as water board chair.

“We are doing this with the best intentions and I stand behind my staff. They are in the midst of it day after day.”

World.title: Do you know “Lucky”? Police can’t ID foreign man in Amsterdam
World.content:
Amsterdam cold case police are appealing for help identifying a man known as “Lucky” who collapsed on the street three years ago after suffering a suspected brain haemorrhage or stroke.

Doctors believe he subsequently developed aphasia, which makes communication nearly impossible. No one has been able to work out who he is or where he came from.

He now lives in a care home in Amsterdam Zuidoost and the only words he still uses are English ones – “nonsense” and “definitely” – which he uses to confirm or deny things. He spoke in an American or Canadian accent, the police say. Beyond that, he cannot talk or communicate at all.

Detectives first began looking into the case in 2023 but every line of inquiry ran into a dead end. The search then passed to the force’s cold case team, where two retired members, named as Ruud and Nel, are now volunteering to find out who he is. Presumably, somewhere his family or friends are looking for him.

A police spokesperson told DutchNews that they have tried to find his identity through DNA databases and with facial recognition technologies, but to no avail. Strict privacy rules limit their powers to access larger data sources where a match could be found, they said.

People who knew him think he may have come from the US or Canada because of his accent. He also may have had a past in Nepal.

A public appeal for information has garnered an “overwhelming” response, police say, with more than 140 tip-offs reported on the first day.

Two nicknames, conflicting clues

Digging into his former social circle, the investigators found that he belonged to a Buddhist community on Middenweg, in the east of the city, where he was known as “Lucky”.

They also learned that he would occasionally have a drink at Soep en Zo, a café on Waterlooplein, where regulars knew him by a different name again: “Chris the Canadian”.

A worker at Soep en Zo who remembers him told DutchNews that he would frequent the shop, often looking shabby and seeming mentally unwell. He always carried a suitcase with him, and would ask for very particular variations of soup, which they would accommodate. He always had money despite his appearance.

Investigators say a lot of the information they’ve gathered is conflicting. “He was supposedly filthy rich, but at the same time he was wandering the streets of Amsterdam,” according to Ruud.

But what the investigators cannot understand is how a person could leave so little trace. “I simply cannot believe that nobody knows who this man really is,” Nel said. “Isn’t it strange that you could perhaps live under the radar in the Netherlands for 20 years?”

“Every person has the right to an identity,” Ruud stressed, “and that includes this man.”

Anyone with potential information on the case can report it to the police here.

World.title: Campaigners call for Amsterdam to pull plug on giant data centre
World.content:
More than 500 people have joined a campaign to stop a huge data centre being built in Amsterdam-Zuid, arguing that it will bring “zero benefits to the area”.

The Dutch government has introduced restrictions on the size of data centres in recent years following criticism from provincial and municipal governments about the strain on the electricity network. Data centres accounted for 4.6% of all electricity use in the Netherlands in 2024.

But the plans to build a 24,000 m2 facility on Amsterdam’s Science Park were submitted by US firm Equinix before the ban, which only applies to new developments, took effect in 2022.

Local residents have also become increasingly vocal in opposing the construction of data centres, while campaign groups Geef Tegengas and Extinction Rebellion both staged demonstrations this summer against a Microsoft project in Amsterdam Sloterdijk.

“There are already enough data centres to keep everything running. This is becoming overkill,” Dylan Bakker of Stop Datacenter Zuidoost told NOS.

Amsterdam city council, which wants to build 8,000 homes in Zuidoost to help relieve the national housing shortage, has attached extra conditions to the site, such as requiring the residual heat from the plant to be used for domestic heating.

Water and electricity

There are also concerns about the strain on water supplies, which have been exacerbated by the summer drought. Equinix said in its planning application that it would need 274 million litres of water a year for the first stage of the project, rising to more than a billion litres when the data centre is complete in 2036.

But the municipality says it would face legal action and penalties if it tore up the permit to build the data center at this stage.

Equinix has said it will only build one of four planned 60-metre data towers initially, until electricity grid operator Tennet can supply enough power.

Tennet warned earlier this year that the network was nearing capacity, leading to a six-month moratorium on new connections in Utrecht.

The complete campus in Zuidoost will consume 779 kWh of electricity a year, almost as much as all the households Amsterdam combined, which currently use 869 kWh.

Michiel Eielts, director of Equinix Benelux, argued that the data centres were an essential part of modern infrastructure. “Every house needs the internet. We need data centres for the growth of our companies, our public services and our security,” he said.

World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data https://t.co/NJX7MBmy3Z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and whom Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the reintroduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices.
